items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the vehicle and traffic law, in relation to the displaying of
a bus driver's credentials while he or she is on duty and the review of his or
her files
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S3450

SPONSOR: STAVISKY
 
TITLE OF BILL:  An act to amend the vehicle and traffic law, in
relation to the displaying of a bus driver's credentials while he or she
is on duty and the review of his or her files

 
PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF THE BILL:

To require the Department of Motor Vehicles to issue a new credential
for individuals qualified to drive a bus under Article 19A of the Vehi-
cle and Traffic Law and to require the display of such credential inside
of a bus while the bus driver is on duty. This would allow consumers and
passengers to verify that their bus driver has met all of the legal
requirements to drive the bus.

To require the Department of Motor Vehicles to perform an annual audit
of motor carriers subject to VTL Article 19A requirements at least once
a year to ensure that motor carriers are in compliance with the law.

 
SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS:

Section 1 of the bill is amended and adds a new subdivision 5 to section
509(b) of the Vehicle and Traffic Law to require bus driver credentials
to always be displayed prominently in the front of the bus while the bus
driver is on duty. The credential must be displayed prominently for
passengers and consumers to see while boarding.

Section 2 of the bill will amend Section 509(m)(1) and add a new subdi-
vision 8 to the Vehicle and Traffic Law to require the Department of
Motor Vehicles to review a motor carrier's records once every year
instead of every three years. The new subdivision 8 added to section
509(m) of the Vehicle and Traffic Law will require the DMV to issue a
new credential annually for bus drivers qualified to drive a bus under
Article 19A, and such credential should be designed to be publically
displayed.

Section 3 of the bill states that the act shall take effect immediately.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

Private charter buses have dramatically increased service within New
York State. Consumers are routinely boarding such buses to visit casinos
and other destinations in and out of New York State. There has been an
increase in the number of accidents involving such buses, and some of
these accidents have involved drivers who were not qualified and/or
properly licensed to drive passenger buses. The public display of a
credential issued by the DMV would allow consumers to know that their
bus driver is properly licensed and qualified. The public display of
said credential is similar to the requirements some municipalities have
for livery drivers and for-hire taxis to display a similar credential,
or for public bus operators who wear a uniform and identifying informa-
tion.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

2018: S 6921 - Referred to Transportation; A 8726 - Referred to Trans-
portation.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

To be determined.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately.

TO REQUIRE THE DEPARTMENT OF MOTOR VEHICLES TO ISSUE A NEW CREDENTIAL
FOR INDIVIDUALS QUALIFIED TO DRIVE A BUS UNDER ARTICLE 19A OF THE VEHI-
CLE AND TRAFFIC LAW AND TO REQUIRE THE DISPLAY OF SUCH CREDENTIAL INSIDE

SION 8 TO THE VEHICLE AND TRAFFIC LAW TO REQUIRE THE DEPARTMENT OF MOTOR

EVERY THREE YEARS. THE NEW SUBDIVISION 8 ADDED TO SECTION.  509(M) OF
THE VEHICLE AND TRAFFIC LAW WILL REQUIRE THE DMV TO ISSUE A NEW CREDEN-
TIAL ANNUALLY FOR BUS DRIVERS QUALIFIED TO DRIVE A BUS UNDER ARTICLE
19A, AND SUCH CREDENTIAL SHOULD BE DESIGNED TO BE PUBLICLY DISPLAYED.

SECTION 3 OF THE BILL STATES THAT THE ACT SHALL TAKE EFFECT IMMEDIATELY.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

PRIVATE CHARTER BUSES HAVE DRAMATICALLY INCREASED SERVICE WITHIN NEW
YORK STATE. CONSUMERS ARE ROUTINELY BOARDING SUCH BUSES TO VISIT CASINOS
AND OTHER DESTINATIONS IN AND OUT OF NEW YORK STATE. THERE HAS BEEN AN
INCREASE IN THE NUMBER OF ACCIDENTS INVOLVING SUCH BUSES, AND SOME OF
THESE ACCIDENTS HAVE INVOLVED DRIVERS WHO WERE NOT QUALIFIED AND/OR
PROPERLY LICENSED TO DRIVE PASSENGER BUSES. THE PUBLIC DISPLAY OF A
CREDENTIAL ISSUED BY THE DMV WOULD ALLOW CONSUMERS TO KNOW THAT THEIR
BUS DRIVER IS PROPERLY LICENSED AND QUALIFIED. THE PUBLIC DISPLAY OF
SAID CREDENTIAL IS SIMILAR TO THE REQUIREMENTS SOME MUNICIPALITIES HAVE
FOR LIVERY DRIVERS AND FOR-HIRE TAXIS TO DISPLAY A SIMILAR CREDENTIAL,
OR FOR PUBLIC BUS OPERATORS WHO WEAR A UNIFORM AND IDENTIFYING INFORMA-
TION.

2018: S 6921 - REFERRED TO TRANSPORTATION; A 8726 - REFERRED TO TRANS-
PORTATION.

TO BE DETERMINED.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
THIS ACT SHALL TAKE EFFECT IMMEDIATELY.

B.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S3450B

SPONSOR: STAVISKY
 
TITLE OF BILL:  An act to amend the vehicle and traffic law, in
relation to the displaying of a bus driver's credentials while he or she
is on duty and the review of his or her files

 
PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF THE BILL:

To require the Department of Motor Vehicles to issue a new credential
for individuals qualified to drive a bus under Article 19A of the Vehi-
cle and Traffic Law and to require the display of such credential inside
of a bus while the bus driver is on duty. This would allow consumers and
passengers to verify that their bus driver has met all of the legal
requirements to drive the bus and that the bus has been properly
inspected and has operating authority.

To require the Department of Motor Vehicles to perform an annual audit
of motor carriers subject to VTL Article 19A requirements at least once
a year to ensure that motor carriers are in compliance with the law.

 
SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS:

Section 1 of the bill is amended and adds a new 509-p of the Vehicle and
Traffic Law to require bus driver credentials, inspection status, and
DOT operating authority to always be displayed prominently in the front
of the bus while the bus driver is on duty. These must be displayed
prominently for passengers and consumers to see while boarding, and must
be displayed where motor carriers perform contract or common carrier
services.

Section 2 of the bill will amend Section 509(m)(1) and add a new subdi-
vision 8 to the Vehicle and Traffic Law to require the Department of
Motor Vehicles to review a motor carrier's records once every year
instead of every three years. The new subdivision 8 added to section
509(m) of the Vehicle and Traffic Law will require the DMV to issue a
new credential annually for bus drivers qualified to drive a bus under
Article 19A, and such credential should be designed to be publically
displayed.

Section 3 of the bill states that the act shall take effect April 1
after being signed into law.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

Private charter buses have dramatically increased service within New
York State. Consumers are routinely boarding such buses to visit casinos
and other destinations in and out of New York State. There has been an
increase in the number of accidents involving such buses, and some of
these accidents have involved drivers who were not qualified and/or
properly licensed to drive passenger buses. The public display of a
credential issued by the DMV would allow consumers to know that their
bus driver is properly licensed and qualified. The public display of
said credential is similar to the requirements some municipalities have
for livery drivers and for-hire taxis to display a similar credential,
or for public bus operators who wear a uniform and identifying informa-
tion.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:
Revised 5/9/19
2018: S.6921 - Referred to Transportation; A 8726 - Referred to Trans-
portation.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

To be determined.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect April 1 after being signed into law.

summary: Requires the display of a bus driver's credentials prominently while he or she is on duty and changes the review of his or her files by the department from every three years to annually.
